thread:
maria-eng: Heads-up — sales + product want a concise runbook for p95 vs p99 choices for Acme. They want tonight's call to have clear tradeoffs (latency floor, throughput, and cost).

darren-sales: Thanks. Acme asked for two SLO options: p95=120ms (aggressive) or p99=300ms (conservative). They also gave expected qps burst ~220.

amy-product: They care most about perceived snappiness for UI flows (p95), but legal requires a p99 contract clause for critical endpoints. Need recommendation on what we can guarantee on Dedicated.

jlee: Quick notes from perf runs this morning: with microbatch=1 we're at p95 ~110ms, p99 ~360ms at 200qps. microbatch=4 raises throughput ~1.8x but p99 jumps to ~520ms. KV cache hit rate~72% on their workload.

sam-ml: Kernel selection mattered: daytime runs with fused-attn kernel reduced median by ~20ms and p95 ~35ms, but didn't help p99 much due to KV miss spikes. Also observed tails from sequence-length variance.

anya: TL;DR for call: offer (A) latency-first: microbatch=1, fused kernels, aggressive prefix caching; expected p95~115ms, p99~360-400ms, throughput ~200qps. (B) throughput-first: microbatch=4, kernel fallback to general path for long seqs; p95~150ms, p99~500ms, throughput ~360qps.

maria-eng: Can we add a short profiling snippet to show where p99 comes from? keeps call concrete.

jlee: Adding the hot-path breakdown I pulled:
```
hot-path breakdown (sample window):
- model forward (fused-attn): median 48ms, p95 82ms, p99 160ms
- kv lookup + cache miss penalty: median 6ms, p95 18ms, p99 210ms
- batching/queueing (microbatch=4): median 12ms, p95 28ms, p99 95ms
- scheduling + context switch: p99 tail adds ~30-60ms in worst bins
```

sam-ml: The kv miss penalty dominates the tail. If we can bump KV hit rate from 72% -> 88% (prefix warmups, client-side sticky routes) p99 drops by ~120-140ms in our tests.

anya: That suggests a hybrid recommendation: commit to p95=120ms on Dedicated with a p99 guardrail at 400ms if customer applies our warmup guidance and uses sticky routing. Otherwise default p99=500ms.

darren-sales: Acme may push back on 500ms. Can we present an "enterprise plus" option: extra reserved GPUs (dedicated pool) + aggressive KV prewarm for $X/month to hit p99 320-350ms?

jlee: Yes, adding reserved capacity reduces scheduling variance and queueing tail; in our sims reserved pool + prewarm -> p99 ~330-360ms at 220qps, cost uplift ~30%.

amy-product: I'll prepare two one-slide tradeoffs and the pricing delta. Keep the tech scarable to 2 bullets each.

maria-eng: For the call, we should surface two engineering risks: (1) long-seq kernel fallback — still a tail risk; (2) KV cold-starts — orchestration needed. Action items: jlee produce 1-page perf note, sam produce config diff for microbatch & kernel selection, anya craft the customer-facing verify steps.

jlee: I'll post the perf note in #eng-runtime in 30m.

sam-ml: I'll paste the example config snippet for the call: 
```yaml
inference_policy:
  microbatch_size: 1 # latency-first
  kernel_priority: [fused-attn, generic]
  kv_cache:
    warmup: true
    prefetch_shards: 2
```

deploy-bot: loadtest/1762504321 started on dedicated-pool-5 — target qps=220, duration=10m

anya: Perfect — we'll use the loadtest numbers in the slide. Call at 11am PT, I'll drop a calendar invite to the Acme thread. :thumbsup:

maria-eng: Thanks all — keep replies short. We need the one-pager by 10:15.

jlee: ack, uploading note in 20.

darren-sales: will prep pricing bullets and negotiation levers.

anya: closing thread — see slides in 40. :rocket:
